body:
While IL GOP officials disparage Trump, say that he’s going to prison if he doesn’t win the election, or avoid talking about him, Trump's lead grows.

View this email in your browser (https://mailchi.mp/fe98ccb966ad/trump-desantis-and-the-caulkins-effect-latest-conservative-updates?e=1cb5fdae9e)
https://www.illinoisreview.com/?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D
Illinois Review eBlast Powered By
https://kasparlaw.co/?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D
https://www.bestdental.org/?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D

IL GOP Official Echoes the Democrats, Suggests Trump Is Running for President to Avoid Jail, in an Interview During GOP Day at the State Fair (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2023/08/il-gop-official-echoes-the-democrats-suggests-trump-is-running-for-president-to-avoid-jail-in-an-interview-during-gop-day-at-the-state-fair.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D)
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2023/08/il-gop-official-echoes-the-democrats-suggests-trump-is-running-for-president-to-avoid-jail-in-an-interview-during-gop-day-at-the-state-fair.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D
Illinois GOP Day at the state fair in Springfield on Thursday, August 17, 2023. (Source: Thomas J. Turney/State Journal-Register)
With less than a week before the first Republican primary debate in Milwaukee, DeSantis campaign supporters and a pro-DeSantis super PAC, are ramping up their attacks on Republican frontrunner President Donald Trump – in a kamikaze-style mission – and Illinois GOP officials, including Republican national committeeman Richard Porter – are taking the bait and feeding the Democratic narrative that Trump is running for president to avoid going to jail.

In an interview at the Illinois GOP Day at the state fair on Thursday in Springfield, Porter – a diehard DeSantis supporter and the chief architect of the failed Richard Irvin for governor campaign, spoke with the
Chicago Tribune (https://www.chicagotribune.com/politics/ct-illinois-republicans-state-fair-20230817-pycxzdra4jez7itg27nktvhv6m-story.html?lctg=443D14D13572C4AB7490B4ED9B&utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email&utm_term=https%3a%2f%2fwww.chicagotribune.com%2fpolitics%2fct-illinois-republicans-state-fair-20230817-pycxzdra4jez7itg27nktvhv6m-story.html&utm_campaign=CT-Breaking-News&utm_content=alert&utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) , where he sounded more like a Democrat than a Republican when discussing the candidacy of the 45th President of the United States.

“I think the most ardent Trumpers recognize that they might love him in their heart, but they know in their head he is not going to win independents in Georgia, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Michigan, New Hampshire, Arizona and Nevada. And that’s what you need to do to become president. And if you don’t become president of the United States, Trump goes to jail.”

Today, in a dialogue with Illinois Review, Porter provided the following comments to clarify his position:
“1) The Democrats have weaponized the justice system. First against Trump associates, and now against Trump himself. This is profoundly wrong and un-American.

2) All but one of the cases are in Democrat-controlled jurisdictions, where Democrats have been racking up convictions unjustly on Trump associates. One of the cases involves a friend of mine who has been sentenced to jail time if he does not prevail on his appeal. This case, like many others, is wrong on the facts and the law, but so far justice is not being done.

3) The only way to stop the injustice of a government weaponized against political opponents is with a strong Republican President, who understands the injustice and is tough and aggressive enough to root it out.

4) Theoretically, that could be Donald Trump himself. But, we know that to become President he must receive a plurality of the votes in enough states to receive a majority of the electoral votes.

5) The swing states have been and are likely to be GA, PA, WI, MI, AZ, and NV. Throw in NH and NC too, one Trump won and the other he lost before.

6) To win these states, a Republican candidate needs to win the independent votes. This is not 2016 — Trump is no longer new. Plus he behaved abysmally after he lost last time — and of course the purpose of these cases is to remind independent voters of Trump’s bad behavior, and to drive Democrat turnout.

7) Why do you think Trump can do better in these states with those people — who are not pro-Trump to start with — than he did in 2020? Or better than candidates that embraced him did in 2018 or 2022? Again — maybe he beats all these charges before Democrat juries in Democrat jurisdictions, but so far it has not worked out well for anyone that these politicized prosecutors went after.

I believe the base case for planning purposes should be that he loses on at least some counts. Better case is he gets the cases delayed until after the election — but if a Republican is not in office, the Democrats will pursue the cases to use Trump’s bad behavior as a screen for their on-going weaponization. Best case is Trump beats them all. Worst case is he’s hammered by a jury or juries.

8) Is Trump therefore the best candidate for us to stop this injustice? I think the answer is no! DeSantis has proven he’s tough, he’s effective, he’s generally great on policy and he gets the problem. He doesn’t need to carry the baggage of the injustice — he’s free to point out how wrong the baggage is.

Florida under DeSantis has become the showpiece of Republican governance. His leadership stands in stark contrast to the Democrats. He’s young, has a great family and he has virtues Republicans generally admire. I think he’s more likely than any other candidate to keep our energized Trump supporters on the team in 2024.

I think it’s unwise for us as a party to ignore the practical implications these unjust cases have on the likely electoral outcome. I understand that Trump is popular in part because he’s become a martyr, done in by the swamp. But our ideals need to live on and we can’t let these politicized prosecutions succeed.

Instead we need to focus on the best strategy for winning, and that’s the only way we can right these systemic wrongs.

We will see how the candidates do in their first outing next week. There are several that are good, but I think DeSantis is likely to stand out. And he has a strong track record of experience; we have seen how he leads. Plus — almost all Republicans like him and respect him, even if many prefer another candidate at the moment.

We need to play to win the general election. Fundamental freedoms and norms essential to the functioning of our Republic will be destroyed by Democrats if we don’t win this election.

To use a baseball analogy, when the starting pitcher is gassed, pull him and put in the young fresh arm. Trump may be the sentimental favorite to many, but someone else needs to step up and make this happen. I think that’s DeSantis — who I believe most would support if Trump were not in the race to start with.
”
Republican House Minority leader Tony McCombie, Dist. 89, didn’t echo Porter’s comments, but during an interview with the Tribune, she tried to avoid talking about the wildly popular former president – even asking, “I’m always so curious as why is it all about Donald Trump? Why don’t we concentrate about what’s going on in Illinois?”

McCombie oversees a deflated House Republican caucus where they are in the super minority – occupying just 40-seats in an 118-seat chamber – meaning Democrats hold a 78-seat majority over McCombie and House Republicans – making GOP voices virtually irrelevant in the state’s capitol.

Perhaps McCombie prefers to talk about her irrelevance in Springfield, instead, since it’s Illinois.

Or maybe
McCombie (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2023/01/breaking-powerful-teachers-union-that-supported-mandates-helped-write-sex-education-standards-donated-to-illinois-republicans.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) prefers to talk about the National Education Association – an organization whose state association in Illinois endorsed (https://ieanea.org/2022/09/19/iea-board-of-directors-recommends-candidates-for-statewide-constitutional-officers/?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) Democrat Gov. JB Pritzker for governor and Democrat Kwame Raoul for attorney general; promoted mandates during the pandemic, and helped write the controversial sex education standards – and donated more than $1.5 million to Illinois House and Senate Republicans since the start of the pandemic through their political action committee, Illinois PAC for Education (IPACE).

The
NEA (https://www.nea.org/nea-today/all-news-articles/sex-education-schools-needs-upgrade?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) also played a critical role in drafting the incredibly controversial National Sexuality Education Standards (https://advocatesforyouth.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/josh-fose-standards-web.pdf?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) , allowing teachers to teach children about gender identity, sexual orientation, hormone blockers and gender expression.

The curriculum has angered parents in Illinois and across the country – and that anger is justified. More than
500 school districts (https://freebeacon.com/campus/illinois-public-schools-opt-out-of-left-wing-sex-ed-standards/?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) in Illinois have exercised their ability to “opt-out,” declining to teach these outrageous sex education standards to children in their classrooms.

And who was the largest Republican recipient of this Democratic money? Illinois House Republican Minority leader Tony McCombie, who received
$119,900 (https://www.elections.il.gov/CampaignDisclosure/ContributionSearchByCommittees.aspx?txtCmteName=ph1j32c0AlKA4iYdvKeJoTM3nPEA0f47I1CCT%2fR2FQNNplLq7whr0mN6ucvRtdSb&ddlCmteNameSearchType=%2fOm8zAJ7f4ioTTB90BLGGijKP5NjRbIx&ddlVendorState=Ry707kcsXsM%3d&ddlContributionType=wOGh3QTPfKqV2YWjeRmjTeStk426RfVK&ddlState=Ry707kcsXsM%3d&ddlFiledDateTime=Ry707kcsXsM%3d&ddlFiledDateTimeThru=Ry707kcsXsM%3d&utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) in donations since 2020.

In Illinois, it’s expected that one of the largest teachers unions would support Democrats. But to support Illinois Republican legislators – including McCombie, whose own constituents oppose every single policy of the Illinois Education Association and their PAC – and for the Republicans to happily accept their contributions – is shocking.

And who suffers? Our children.

While IL GOP officials either disparage Trump, say that he’s going to prison if he doesn’t win the election, or completely avoid talking about him, altogether – Trump continues to go up in the polls – widening his lead over DeSantis by over 40 points.

This publication agrees with McCombie – let’s talk about Illinois – because she has a lot of explaining to do.

The Caulkins Effect: Effingham County Court Unexpectedly Dismisses DeVore's Cases Challenging the Assault Weapons Ban (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2023/08/the-caulkins-effect-effingham-county-court-unexpectedly-dismisses-devores-cases-challenging-assault-weapons-ban.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D)
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2023/08/the-caulkins-effect-effingham-county-court-unexpectedly-dismisses-devores-cases-challenging-assault-weapons-ban.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D
IL State Rep. Dan Caulkins (R), in an undated photo.
On Wednesday afternoon, the Effingham County Court entered a dismissal of the consolidated litigations brought by former Republican AG candidate Tom DeVore on behalf of more than 7000 Illinoisans against Gov. JB Pritzker’s assault weapons ban. The dismissal was entered sua sponte–on the Court’s own accord–without any request by the AG’s office and without any opportunity for the plaintiffs to be heard. The Court’s dismissal simply cites the recent Illinois Supreme Court (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2023/08/breaking-illinois-supreme-court-rules-4-3-against-dan-caulkins-assault-weapons-ban-case-says-ban-doesnt-violate-state-constitution-in-another-blow-to-gun-advocates.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) ruling in a similar, but unrelated case brought by IL State Rep. Dan Caulkins.

As Illinois Review
previously reported (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2023/08/gov-jb-pritzker-buys-time-with-defeat-over-caulkins-assault-weapons-ban-challenge-but-devores-tro-and-challenge-against-the-ban-continues.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) , the Illinois Supreme Court ruled against Caulkins’ as there was nothing in the record to prove that the exempted classes of people in the assault weapons ban were not justified. In February, the Illinois Supreme Court declined to consolidate (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2023/02/illinois-supreme-court-denies-consolidation-of-state-rep-caulkins-lawsuit-against-gov-pritzkers-assault-weapons-ban-with-the-devore-cases.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) Caulkins’ case with DeVore’s cases on the basis that Caulkins’ case was procedurally distinct. Notably, Caulkins’ case was based only on legal issues, and as the Illinois Supreme Court stated in its opinion, Caulkins had waived all other challenges to the assault weapons ban.

DeVore intends to seek reconsideration of the Effingham County Court’s dismissal and to appeal the matter if necessary. His press release follows.
https://devorelawoffices.com/press-release-assualt-weapons-ban-case-dismissal/?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=fa58b03d13-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_08_18_01_47&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-fa58b03d13-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D

name: Greta Kemp Martin
subject: Ending our runaway corruption
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Greta Martin for AG
body:
Peter, I’m not asking for money today. This is a longer email about how I would tackle corruption and fraud in our state, and I hope you’ll take the time to read it all the way through.

No one is above the law, especially politicians and those who are supposed to be serving the public with integrity. So why have we seen zero prosecutions for nearly $100 million intended for families in need that were given away to celebrity athletes and wealthy insiders?

It’s high time we had an Attorney General in Mississippi willing to take on corruption and hold those who misuse positions of trust or taxpayer dollars accountable for their actions, including by tackling the lack of transparency and accountability.

As your AG, I will investigate and prosecute public and political corruption, fight for public transparency, and work to rebuild trust in government. It is crucial for the public to have trust in their elected officials and confidence in the systems that serve them.

To crack down on corruption, I would implement a comprehensive strategy aimed at preventing and prosecuting instances of fraud against the government. This strategy would involve several key measures that are glaringly absent from our current AG’s practices.

Sharing information and insights can help identify patterns of fraudulent activities more effectively. That’s why establishing strong lines of communication and collaboration between different government agencies, law enforcement entities, and relevant stakeholders is crucial.

Issues like campaign finance law violations are rarely even investigated. I would create specialized investigative units within the Attorney General's office dedicated to identifying, investigating, and prosecuting fraud against the government. I’m not allowing folks who have stolen millions in state funds or abused our legal processes to walk away scot-free.

I would strengthen whistleblower protections for individuals with knowledge of fraudulent activities to come forward without fear of retaliation, and Implement comprehensive audit and monitoring programs to regularly review government programs and contracts for any signs of irregularities or potential fraud.

And finally, I would pursue the recovery of funds lost due to fraud, ensuring that taxpayer dollars are spent how they were intended.

Peter, these are common-sense measures that our current AG frankly doesn’t care to take the time to implement. And our state deserves better.

I’m running for Mississippi Attorney General because people deserve someone who will show up to do the job they were elected to do. I’ll fight tirelessly for Mississippians, just as I’ve done my entire career, to uphold our laws and ensure everyone gets a fair shake in our justice system.

If you’ve read this far, thank you. Being Attorney General isn’t a glamorous job – there are a lot of nitty-gritty details to mind, and the issues aren’t always the most interesting to learn about. But they’re issues that affect our day-to-day lives, and they deserve an AG who will give it their all. That’s what I’ll do as your Attorney General.

Thanks so much for standing with me,

Greta

--

Greta Kemp Martin was born, raised, and educated in Mississippi. She is an active member of the Mississippi Bar, and currently works as the Litigation Director for Disability Rights Mississippi, the protection and advocacy agency for the state. As Attorney General, Greta will fight for the rights of everyday Mississippians, and stand up for the working people of this state.

name: Josh Shapiro
subject: The first of its kind in America
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY SHAPIRO FOR PENNSYLVANIA
body:
Derek – Pennsylvania just created a new worker training initiative that is the **first of its kind in America.** The Commonwealth Workforce Transformation Program will utilize federal infrastructure money to expand Pennsylvania’s skilled workforce – ensuring that future critical infrastructure projects will have the prepared and trained workers they need. **This program is a _big_ one – it can provide training for up to _10,000_ workers statewide.** I’m serious about infrastructure, and this program will ensure our Commonwealth has enough resources and workers to build the roads, bridges, and trains we’ll need in the decades ahead. Whether it’s through workforce training programs like this, or by waiving the college-education requirement for the vast majority of state jobs, **I’m proud to support working Pennsylvanians in every way I can.** Since day one as Governor, I’ve fought to put hard-working Pennsylvanians first, and I couldn’t be more proud of our results so far. **But we can’t become complacent now – not when the far-right wants to undo all of the progress we’ve made together in Pennsylvania.** [_**Please, chip in $10 or more right now to help my team and me continue putting working Pennsylvanians first – we can’t afford to lose this progress.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68304564/422606775/223969246?refcode=email_081823_Workforce-training&amount=10&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0ZWEwYTI1OS1mNjNkLWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=xrn3ebCcbnBstl86yusLQA7D-su4zqw0BfRbC-iTQLU=) _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | | [Donate $10 →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68304565/422606776/223969246?refcode=email_081823_Workforce-training&amount=10&express_lane=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0ZWEwYTI1OS1mNjNkLWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=xrn3ebCcbnBstl86yusLQA7D-su4zqw0BfRbC-iTQLU=)

subject: Why Texas Is So Important

body:
Peter: This race is bigger than defeating Ted Cruz. Our
Democratic Senate majority and the White House are on the line in 2024.

The future of our democracy and so many of our fundamental rights, from
voting to reproductive freedom, depend on Democrats winning.
Unfortunately, the 2024 Senate map strongly favors Republicans.

But here's the thing: Experts at CNN and FiveThirtyEight are calling Texas
our BEST pickup opportunity – and if we can flip this seat, Democrats are
virtually guaranteed to defend the Senate!

[ https://act.charlesbooker.org/go/18996?t=1001&akid=3502%2E346206%2EKLa08l ]Please, split a donation of $25 or more between my campaign and Charles
Booker before our midnight deadline to help Colin Allred beat Ted Cruz,
flip Texas blue and defend our Democratic Senate majority! →

Our chances have never looked better to flip Texas: This team raised more
in our first 24 hours than Ted Cruz raised in the first three months of
the year, causing Inside Elections to update their official Texas ranking
from "Solid Republican" to "Battleground." People are calling this the
political fight of Ted Cruz's life.

That’s why Mitch McConnell, GOP mega donors and shady special interests
are going to spend whatever it takes to save Ted Cruz and defeat Colin.

But we've got to keep up our momentum, friend, and that's where you come
in. We have an ambitious $150,000 daily fundraising goal because in a
battleground race, money could be the difference between winning and
losing. Right now, we're falling short, and we're counting on you to help
close the gap.

#
Peter — the grassroots movement we’re building to defeat Josh Hawley, flip this U.S. Senate seat, and take back power for everyday people is already the boldest campaign in Missouri history. **Please let me explain.**

I can’t accept a status quo where politicians who take massive donations from Big Ag tell us it’s normal for billionaires in China and Brazil to buy up our farmland and put hard-working family farmers out of business. And I won’t stand for another twenty years of members of Congress who’ve never worn a uniform sacrificing American lives and tax dollars on forever wars, while refusing to invest into the everyday people who make our country strong.
Out-of-touch elites like Josh Hawley have spent decades wasting our money on tax breaks and subsidies for Wall Street, Big Pharma, Big Tech, and just about everything else that’s gutting our country.
They’re willing to lie, cheat, and steal from the American people to protect the massive corporations and mega-donors who own their careers — and they’ll even raise their fist to look strong before they start running from threats to our democracy.
**We don’t need any more frauds in Congress.** That’s why I’m running for U.S. Senate. More than just fighting to codify protections for abortion access — **I’m running to end the filibuster so we can actually get it done.**
More than just banning insider trading among members of Congress and their families — **I’m running to put them in jail if they steal from us.**
More than just breaking up Big Pharma — **I’m running to prosecute the insulin cartels who are killing people.**
And more than just rejecting corporate PAC money — **I’m running to abolish corporate PACs altogether.**

My efforts to protect voting rights extend past our district.

Friend,
_“Being one of 14 children during back to school season was very difficult for my immigrant parents. We would definitely use our backpacks for multiple years and share clothes, but there was always a need for new supplies like folders, paper, and notebooks, that helped us start the school year successfully. I still remember, as the eldest, asking my parents for the calculator I needed for algebra and geometry. They couldn't afford one so I borrowed one from a classmate until a teacher got me one._
_It is so important that we come together as a loving community to help families who may be struggling to ensure their child has everything they need this school year. Please check out how you can help below.”_
_\- Rashida_

Rashida Tlaib fights for working class families around the country through transformative policies like the End Childhood Poverty Act. subject: legalizing marijuana in Pennsylvania

body:
Team,

In 2017, when I became the first statewide elected official in Pennsylvania to support legalizing and taxing recreational marijuana, I knew I was going to ruffle some feathers.

_But I did it because it was the right thing to do._

Legalizing marijuana would:

💰Generate $581M tax revenue for PA
⚕️Allow veterans to have medical covered through TRICARE
⚖️ Prevent the costly incarceration of thousands of Pennsylvanians for simple possession

Look, I believe marijuana in Pennsylvania ought to be safe, legal, and regulated. [**If you agree, will you sign my petition to support legalization? →**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68306872/422615097/1548860827?refcode=email_081823_legalizemarijuana_t2&utm_campaign=email_081823_legalizemarijuana_t2&source=email_081823_legalizemarijuana_t2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NTE3NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYmQ0NjUxNi1mZDNkLWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4OwhVlgq24vsTEu-XsbD_zDyBTDX718BMeaTcSpbJpk=&emci=c5d492ce-fc3d-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&emdi=abd46516-fd3d-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&ceid=10203249) | | [Sign the Petition →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68306874/422615099/1548860827?refcode=email_081823_legalizemarijuana_t2&utm_campaign=email_081823_legalizemarijuana_t2&source=email_081823_legalizemarijuana_t2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NTE3NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYmQ0NjUxNi1mZDNkLWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4OwhVlgq24vsTEu-XsbD_zDyBTDX718BMeaTcSpbJpk=&emci=c5d492ce-fc3d-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&emdi=abd46516-fd3d-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&ceid=10203249)

I’ll be upfront: **I know legalizing marijuana could be a useful tool in fighting the opioid epidemic.**

When my father was injured in Vietnam, he battled a painkiller addiction for years and ultimately ended up in jail. It nearly destroyed him and my family–so this issue is personal.

And to be clear: I’m not trying to play doctor, I’m just looking at the numbers:

For people in severe pain, marijuana is a better path than opioids. Every state that has legalized marijuana saw a *drop* in opioid addiction. _There are 25 percent fewer deaths from opioid overdose in states that permit medical marijuana use._

clean_body: Team, In 2017, when I became the first statewide elected official in Pennsylvania to support legalizing and taxing recreational marijuana, I knew I was going to ruffle some feathers. When my father was injured in Vietnam, he battled a painkiller addiction for years and ultimately ended up in jail. It nearly destroyed him and my family–so this issue is personal. And to be clear: I’m not trying to play doctor, I’m just looking at the numbers: For people in severe pain, marijuana is a better path than opioids. Every state that has legalized marijuana saw a drop in opioid addiction. There are 25 percent fewer deaths from opioid overdose in states that permit medical marijuana use. As your next Attorney General, I will continue the fight to end the opioid crisis. For generations, Hawaiians have shared in their culture with us on Maui, and now it's our turn to help. [**Join me in supporting the Maui Food Bank, an organization that is actively providing crucial assistance to those affected by this tragedy.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68307021/422615685/1336115072?refcode=2023-08-18-maui&recurring=&amount=3&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=41f180c3-fd3d-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQxNjIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDFmMTgwYzMtZmQzZC1lZTExLWEzZjEtMDAyMjQ4MzJlYjczIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=BFBb5sOGvd7lOPce1Woic0yUNeaJoJlCeCz3HvyfiOg=) Your contribution will help ensure that basic necessities reach those in need and help rebuild the spirit of Lāhainā. [Support Maui Food Bank](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68307022/422615686/1336115072?refcode=2023-08-18-maui&recurring=&amount=3&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=41f180c3-fd3d-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQxNjIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDFmMTgwYzMtZmQzZC1lZTExLWEzZjEtMDAyMjQ4MzJlYjczIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=BFBb5sOGvd7lOPce1Woic0yUNeaJoJlCeCz3HvyfiOg=) **While Lāhainā holds significance to many of us through fond memories of family vacations, special events, and stunning travel photos, the cultural significance of this community runs deep.** **Lāhainā was once the capital of the Hawaiian Kingdom during the early 19th century.** It served as a political, economic, and cultural hub, where ali'i (royalty) and important leaders gathered — including the reign of King Kamehameha III, who established the first written constitution of the Hawaiian Kingdom in Lāhainā in 1840. Lāhainā's role as a meeting point for cultures and civilizations led to the sharing of knowledge, traditions, and practices, contributing to the unique cultural blend that defines modern Hawaiian identity. **The town is home to some of the most significant artistic and spiritual sites for Hawaiians** , including the ancient temple, Hale Pi'ilani Heiau. Heiaus were places of worship, offering, and ceremony, and they played a central role in Hawaiian religious practices. Lāhainā has a rich tradition of arts and music, including hula, mele, and other artistic expressions. Its vibrant art scene has bolstered the preservation of Hawaiian cultural practices. **The town's natural harbor made it a significant center for trade and commerce** , and was a prominent whaling port during the 19th century. Hawaiians engaged in the exchange of goods, further connecting them with neighboring islands and cultures. Beyond Front Street, it is Lāhainā's cultural significance as a historical, spiritual, artistic, and communal center for native Hawaiians that makes its rehabilitation and preservation vital to ensuring the continued understanding and appreciation of Hawaiian heritage. Friend, I want to personally thank you for always standing with me as we take on the toughest fights in Washington.

Thank you for having my back when we fought for **health care coverage for 9/11 first responders** and **expanded benefits for veterans** exposed to toxic burn pits. We must ensure that our heroes get the care that they need.
Thank you for supporting my hard-won legislation that **empowers survivors of sexual assault** in the military to seek justice. Together, we took on the Pentagon to win reforms that will create a fairer system for service members.
Thank you for never giving up the fight to **make gun trafficking a federal crime.** After 13 years of advocacy, late nights, whipping votes, my legislation was finally passed in last year's Bipartisan Safer Communities Act. Already, we're stopping the flow of illegal guns into New York.
Thank you for your continued commitment to family rights and gender equity. With your support, I have spent the last decade fighting for **national paid family leave** for all workers. And now, I'm proud to lead the charge to add the **Equal Rights Amendment** to our Constitution — which would finally give us the legal basis to restore reproductive rights across the country.
**My record is about winning real results for the families I swore to serve — not for corporations or megadonors. And none of that would be possible without your continued, tireless support.**
But here's the bad news: Republicans are emboldened after their historic victories in New York last year. **Now, they're laying the groundwork for an even bigger red wave in 2024 — and they're directly targeting my seat.** I refuse to accept a single cent from corporate PACs, so I'm relying on grassroots donors like you to compete with their right-wing megadonors.
**[_Please, friend, you've stood by me so many times before and I'm counting on you to have my back again. disclaimer_text: Paid for by Laura Friedman for Congress
body:
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68307302/422616602/62647395?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM1MzYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDU3YzdkYWUtZmYzZC1lZTExLWEzZjEtMDAyMjQ4MzJlYjczIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=_mMCOQIq-aBG_HZsbDs00ALDJMKw8KlvEk__Q6eZsSA=) Friend, this may surprise you, but when I'm meeting with constituents I get more questions about water conservation than almost any other issue.

We enjoyed a historic wet winter season, but it was only last year that we nearly depleted the state’s reservoirs and groundwater resources after a multi-year drought.

When it comes to water resiliency, praying for rain isn't a strategy. That's why I introduced (and helped pass) Assembly Bill 1572 which phases out the use of potable water for growing ornamental lawns and “nonfunctional turf” for industrial and commercial properties.

**It's time to say goodbye to grass that’s just for looks, and it turns out the Los Angeles Times Editorial Board agrees!**
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68307303/422616603/-1652506406?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM1MzYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDU3YzdkYWUtZmYzZC1lZTExLWEzZjEtMDAyMjQ4MzJlYjczIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=_mMCOQIq-aBG_HZsbDs00ALDJMKw8KlvEk__Q6eZsSA=&emci=253785a8-ff3d-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&emdi=d57c7dae-ff3d-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&ceid=8447100) | ****[Read the Editorial](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68307304/422616604/-1652506406?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM1MzYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDU3YzdkYWUtZmYzZC1lZTExLWEzZjEtMDAyMjQ4MzJlYjczIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=_mMCOQIq-aBG_HZsbDs00ALDJMKw8KlvEk__Q6eZsSA=&emci=253785a8-ff3d-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&emdi=d57c7dae-ff3d-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&ceid=8447100)****
---

We waste billions (yes, billions with b) of gallons of water on nonfunctional turf each year. And I’m not talking about your lawn at home or grass at parks and picnic grounds -- which we love and need. Decorative turf is what you'd find in a street median or in front of an office building. Outside of hogging precious water, it has no real use.

My bill is one important step among many that we must take in order to protect our water supply in the long run. I'm proud that it passed in the state assembly, and I'll continue to advocate until it's signed into law.

Laura
**Before you click away.**

clean_body: | = Friend, this may surprise you, but when I'm meeting with constituents I get more questions about water conservation than almost any other issue. We enjoyed a historic wet winter season, but it was only last year that we nearly depleted the state’s reservoirs and groundwater resources after a multi-year drought. When it comes to water resiliency, praying for rain isn't a strategy. That's why I introduced (and helped pass) Assembly Bill 1572 which phases out the use of potable water for growing ornamental lawns and “nonfunctional turf” for industrial and commercial properties. It's time to say goodbye to grass that’s just for looks, and it turns out the Los Angeles Times Editorial Board agrees! | ** We waste billions (yes, billions with b) of gallons of water on nonfunctional turf each year. And I’m not talking about your lawn at home or grass at parks and picnic grounds -- which we love and need. Decorative turf is what you'd find in a street median or in front of an office building. Outside of hogging precious water, it has no real use. My bill is one important step among many that we must take in order to protect our water supply in the long run. I'm proud that it passed in the state assembly, and I'll continue to advocate until it's signed into law. Laura Before you click away. | | _Image courtesy of WBIR_ It was an honor and privilege to attend the [groundbreaking](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=25406d21ce4e4c719b36a1ec0591acda&_e=SDyBfVmO34HB5IVu7sPNpCI5fC9RL4cGEeSxoQtIu7JdFlgN41j_cfMZruapPMuWSVakJOuamYuNIpE4va1MbHkL08ac_QryfaTUpyBy81NydVgFcRhRjlg-O0vTNehSFppg7k4Dj8SXJ5bKEqsewZmr6Nw2BZ1VE9gweTVHgjk3VAgCki8_R_kFFUXi2pC7SKqZ3_JBH1a4AqKTBZznF1V-JnSTW-mxwKgwBJ15NqRKJgnu4DU8WtlfaLgpwaVUQ24kjqcTGX81mQhBlmY1NgXXnFgoUsBq1PxTswfUrEGG31BZF-jZyu23RaD6x8F60RBIlLQkHmG29wRqw05EIJ5MwNbFSiX4Cg9ss5ZFjPA%3D) of Liberty Place, a supportive housing development for veterans. This is the Knoxville Community Development Center’s first housing site that will be designated specifically for those who bravely served our country. This effort is a part of the HUD-Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing voucher program, which is a joint effort to move veterans out of homelessness and into permanent housing. At Liberty Place, veterans will pay 30% of their income toward the rent, but anything they can’t afford above that will be funded through the federal voucher. In addition to 32 units, the VA will have an office onsite to help coordinate medical and community resources. I’m incredibly proud to be a part of this project. I went to bat to secure a [$2 million earmark](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=25406d21ce4e4c719b36a1ec0591acda&_e=SDyBfVmO34HB5IVu7sPNpHs5XrDqEhI1z_CCVucc4t2-9K7YDfMbUyuLapG4P9aImVU_B8SkTBm0Kcr4zynM_dpf7a47KZQw_mBNRiV9wQi8AKOw6fu4SiklH9cVWH82YHCjgU5b8HLDxf4PHw_HroxSazlAT6bK-tx_Os_7Ev-YRFfC7Eeptr_SgK_CugN88os1HtL-GeC80xgn4PCIzS5ZIBDUYfOmhfHnkDIzhecDMwUKO6mXH2Koe2OAxpKSsiSKemg4S9DR2yefvVD49RYBfOpMJoBka4GJup-H-DKVy9CwbF__fWNnZkqlEArA) for Liberty Place because I believe THIS is what your tax dollars should be paying for. Our veterans served and sacrificed for our country, and we need to take care of them in return. Liberty Place provides a roof over their heads and brings them some much-needed services. I look forward to attending the official opening of Liberty Place to thank our veterans personally.

## Coming To Tulsa This Sepetember

In less than a month **Lara Trump** will be joining me at [Sheridan.Church](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=946009.382.1.b8eb733574073f4b54cc22809a0097b6) in Tulsa, OK for [IGNITE 2023](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=946009.383.1.bc55d0235c1f522789c6c2e67944af77) and **Kash Patel** (_former Chief of Staff for President Trump_) will be joining us that night to give exclusive insights to what is happening in America right now!
Stay tuned for future announcements of other guests joining us in Tulsa this September...
[IGNITE](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=946009.384.1.e11ed789cb92966cdd1ed544b95eca00) is an annual conference at [Sheridan.Church](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=946009.385.1.8983a23b6ad12e7ce9100a138073dbda) with _powerful worship_ , _dynamic speakers_ and a _community of believers on fire for God_.
**Dates** : September 10-13
**Speakers** :
-Lara Trump
-Kash Patel
-Dr. Randy Caldwell
-Bishop Darrell Hines
-David Ring
**Location** : [Sheridan.Church](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=946009.386.1.93c69c08f90bdf99092f01fda15e8ef0) New Campus in Tulsa: 7901 E 41st St Tulsa, OK
**Cost** : FREE
**Seating** : LIMITED
**RSVP** : [www.sheridan.church/ignite23](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=946009.387.1.c4422f380d68b85a73e60d1c9876dcc1)
After the service at [Sheridan.Church](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=946009.388.1.1d2c1da076c16d6514fc00d67e3583ef) on Sunday, September 10, there is a dinner event with Lara Trump & Kash Patel that you can be apart of.
Get your ticket to have dinner with Lara Trump: [www.sheridan.church/ignite23](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=946009.389.1.03d63486dbe17ee8eba6f14ddfd7ae14)

## Sheridan.Church Tulsa Is MOVING!
---
| [ ](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=946009.392.1.f0d782f6023e4a29af9f42bbb1d5a9a5)

The last three years have been more than interesting...
In the midst of all the craziness, we have seen **tremendous growth** at [Sheridan.Church](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=946009.393.1.d5841775e42eb5bb359ce83bad8df5fd). We have currently maxed out our facility in Tulsa with two services every Sunday.
Last year, we were blessed to acquire 14 acres in South Tulsa but that did not solve our immediate need.
I am excited to share with you that [Sheridan.Church](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=946009.394.1.ff9161467fdf5f873fe97533d1a9c286) closed on the purchase of the historic **Caravan Nightclub** in Tulsa, OK.
Features of the new facility:
**-Auditorium will seat 700+**
**-Separate Kids & Youth Wing**
**-Over 400 parking spaces**
We are aiming to have our FIRST service there on Sunday, September 3 at 10am.
In order to do this we are needing to raise $130,000 to complete Phase 1 of the buildout to make the space functional.
I would like for you to pray and consider partnering with us to see this **incredible story of a former tavern becoming a tabernacle in Tulsa**.
You can watch this short video to see what the Caravan Nightclub looks like right now:[https://youtu.be/aq9FDBtTcvA](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=946009.395.1.0d927c1f5e64121f7bdddea65372bdaf)
You can partner with [Sheridan.Church](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=946009.396.1.06029441e6f4329c98051202c59fb755) by visiting: [www.sheridan.church/give](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=946009.397.1.8d6fa771f847d7fbcf122d6a21a9a46f)
I am very grateful for your support!
Thank you,
Jackson Lahmeyer

body:
August 18th marks over 100 years since the ratification of the 19th Amendment – the landmark piece of legislation that gave women the opportunity to vote.
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68308978/422622591/-235809255?refcode=em_eng_2023.08.18_b2_cd_all&amount=3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjU0MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MWU3NjIyMC0wNzNlLWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=NeK6xTSfZ5mBGASLdnPuWhKbRRxgokmsHjgoRhyLSG8=) Derek, today is a historic day. **August 18th marks over 100 years since the ratification of the 19th Amendment** – the landmark piece of legislation that gave women the right to vote.

Of course, the amendment was not perfect in its initial passing. Only white women would be allowed to vote until 35 years later, with the passage of the _Voting Rights Act of 1965_ expanding voting rights to all Americans, regardless of skin color.

**It’s a stark reminder that rings true today: Even with as far as our great nation has come, there is still work to be done to live up to our democratic values.**

Today, our voting rights are under attack. The far-right wants to diminish the power of the people because they know that when working folks show up at the polls, their anti-worker, anti-union, anti-choice, and anti-American agendas get voted out.

subject: Special access to National Honey Bee Day match
body:
| | | | | [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/e_s17_main_cobrandedemail_c3)
---|---|---

| | We have a 'Five-Alarm Fire' when it comes to the future of bees, insect pollinators, and our planet. We’re using National Honey Bee Day to help put it out! Because you are a dedicated member, I am reaching out to you early. I know you won't want to miss this opportunity to do your part to reach our important goal! Why? Because many wild bee species are on the brink of extinction. And key factors in their decline are toxic pesticides produced by companies like Bayer-Monsanto. Even honeybees are facing serious declines -- _**with annual colony losses in the U.S. reaching nearly 50%!**_ This National Honey Bee Day, there’s never been a better time to take action. To help boost our efforts, _**a generous group of donors is matching gifts in honor of National Honey Bee Day, up to our critical $107,000 goal -- but only until midnight tomorrow. **_ Because you are a critical supporter, we have given you early access to help set the pace for National Honey Bee Day: | [EARLY NATIONAL HONEY BEE DAY ACCESS FOR dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://us.engagingnetworks.app/page/email/click/10012/1936139?email=RepJ2ZGQKX6xm5Aey7FwClESkN1MQhKC&campid=UI6tX83ZqbKZkArzVWMSmA==)
---
It's no secret that many critical pollinators are teetering on the edge. And since 1 out of every 3 bites of food we eat is thanks to pollinators, **the situation is dire. **
We’ve already seen shocking declines in just the last two decades: **87% of Rusty-Patched Bumblebees, 89% of American Bumblebees, and 93% of Western Bumblebees have disappeared.** Some are completely gone in several states!
But Big Ag acts like this isn’t a big deal. They continue to produce bee-killing pesticides, making U.S. agriculture _**nearly 48 times more toxic**_ to insects than it was in the 1990s.
Pollinators and our planet don’t deserve to die like this. There are better, more sustainable options when it comes to our food system. But the only way to stop Big Ag and its toxic pesticides is together, Friend. Don’t miss this opportunity to DOUBLE your impact and fight for vulnerable pollinators and the planet before it’s too late!
**This National Honey Bee Day, bees and our planet need your help. Please, donate $27 or more before midnight and have your donation matched -- dollar for dollar.**
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_
[Donate $27 immediately](https://us.engagingnetworks.app/page/email/click/10012/1936140?email=RepJ2ZGQKX6xm5Aey7FwClESkN1MQhKC&campid=UI6tX83ZqbKZkArzVWMSmA==)
---
[Donate $50 immediately](https://us.engagingnetworks.app/page/email/click/10012/1936141?email=RepJ2ZGQKX6xm5Aey7FwClESkN1MQhKC&campid=UI6tX83ZqbKZkArzVWMSmA==)
---
[Donate $100 immediately](https://us.engagingnetworks.app/page/email/click/10012/1936142?email=RepJ2ZGQKX6xm5Aey7FwClESkN1MQhKC&campid=UI6tX83ZqbKZkArzVWMSmA==)
---
[Donate another amount](https://us.engagingnetworks.app/page/email/click/10012/1936143?email=RepJ2ZGQKX6xm5Aey7FwClESkN1MQhKC&campid=UI6tX83ZqbKZkArzVWMSmA==)
---
Why is it so important to save bees? Well, the facts speak for themselves: bees are ecosystem engineers. They are pivotal in supporting healthy habitats for birds, insects, and mammals. And bees and other pollinators are vital for a whopping __**75% of food crops**__ , like fruits, nuts, and vegetables.
But bees are dying at alarming rates. And toxic pesticides -- like Bayer-Monsanto's neonicotinoids are among the biggest contributors to the massive declines of bees and other pollinators. As pesticide usage increases year over year, bee populations continue to decline.
Bees that come in contact with neonics can face horrible fates. The pesticides can impact bees' ability to navigate and reproduce, and even KILL BEES ON CONTACT. They're also the most widely used insecticides in agriculture.
But the damage doesn’t end with bees, Friend: Neonicotinoids have been found in the very food we eat. And they can’t be washed off. What’s worse, these dangerous chemicals can be harmful to human health.**They’ve been linked to health impacts like birth defects of the heart and brain, hormone disruption, and autism.**
Big Ag companies like Bayer-Monsanto keep producing bee-killing pesticides for profit. These corporations are doubling down on their destructive path. That’s why we have to take action now to stop them. But we can’t fight the pesticide industry and save the bees without your help!
**Vulnerable pollinators and the planet need you more than ever: Donate $27 today in honor of National Honey Bee Day and make DOUBLE the impact!**
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_
[Donate $27 immediately](https://us.engagingnetworks.app/page/email/click/10012/1936140?email=RepJ2ZGQKX6xm5Aey7FwClESkN1MQhKC&campid=UI6tX83ZqbKZkArzVWMSmA==)
---
[Donate $50 immediately](https://us.engagingnetworks.app/page/email/click/10012/1936141?email=RepJ2ZGQKX6xm5Aey7FwClESkN1MQhKC&campid=UI6tX83ZqbKZkArzVWMSmA==)

---
Friends of the Earth runs strategic campaigns to eliminate toxic pesticides from our environment. We're pushing garden retailers like Home Depot and Lowe's and supermarkets like Kroger to get these pesticides off their shelves and out of their products. And we’re working to pass policies that ban toxic pesticides in key states and nationally.
Our National Honey Bee Day goal means so much to our organization and the planet. We know you recognize how high the stakes are. That’s why we chose you to be part of this select group for early match access. When you make your early-bird membership donation, you'll be ensuring we can mobilize on the ground, keep pressure on legislators, work to prevent the insect apocalypse from getting worse, and do all that we can to protect our planet.

clean_body: | | | | | ---|---|--- | | We have a 'Five-Alarm Fire' when it comes to the future of bees, insect pollinators, and our planet. We’re using National Honey Bee Day to help put it out! Because you are a dedicated member, I am reaching out to you early. I know you won't want to miss this opportunity to do your part to reach our important goal! Why? Because many wild bee species are on the brink of extinction. And key factors in their decline are toxic pesticides produced by companies like Bayer-Monsanto. Even honeybees are facing serious declines -- with annual colony losses in the U.S. reaching nearly 50%! This National Honey Bee Day, there’s never been a better time to take action. To help boost our efforts, a generous group of donors is matching gifts in honor of National Honey Bee Day, up to our critical $107,000 goal -- but only until midnight tomorrow. Because you are a critical supporter, we have given you early access to help set the pace for National Honey Bee Day: | == It's no secret that many critical pollinators are teetering on the edge. And since 1 out of every 3 bites of food we eat is thanks to pollinators, the situation is dire. We’ve already seen shocking declines in just the last two decades: 87% of Rusty-Patched Bumblebees, 89% of American Bumblebees, and 93% of Western Bumblebees have disappeared. Some are completely gone in several states! But Big Ag acts like this isn’t a big deal. They continue to produce bee-killing pesticides, making U.S. agriculture nearly 48 times more toxic to insects than it was in the 1990s. Pollinators and our planet don’t deserve to die like this. There are better, more sustainable options when it comes to our food system. But the only way to stop Big Ag and its toxic pesticides is together, Friend. Don’t miss this opportunity to DOUBLE your impact and fight for vulnerable pollinators and the planet before it’s too late! This National Honey Bee Day, bees and our planet need your help. Please, donate $27 or more before midnight and have your donation matched -- dollar for dollar. If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: == == == == Why is it so important to save bees? Well, the facts speak for themselves: bees are ecosystem engineers. They are pivotal in supporting healthy habitats for birds, insects, and mammals. And bees and other pollinators are vital for a whopping 75% of food crops , like fruits, nuts, and vegetables. But bees are dying at alarming rates. And toxic pesticides -- like Bayer-Monsanto's neonicotinoids are among the biggest contributors to the massive declines of bees and other pollinators. As pesticide usage increases year over year, bee populations continue to decline. Bees that come in contact with neonics can face horrible fates. The pesticides can impact bees' ability to navigate and reproduce, and even KILL BEES ON CONTACT. They're also the most widely used insecticides in agriculture. But the damage doesn’t end with bees, Friend: Neonicotinoids have been found in the very food we eat. And they can’t be washed off. What’s worse, these dangerous chemicals can be harmful to human health.They’ve been linked to health impacts like birth defects of the heart and brain, hormone disruption, and autism. Big Ag companies like Bayer-Monsanto keep producing bee-killing pesticides for profit. These corporations are doubling down on their destructive path. That’s why we have to take action now to stop them. But we can’t fight the pesticide industry and save the bees without your help! Vulnerable pollinators and the planet need you more than ever: Donate $27 today in honor of National Honey Bee Day and make DOUBLE the impact! And we’re working to pass policies that ban toxic pesticides in key states and nationally. Our National Honey Bee Day goal means so much to our organization and the planet. We know you recognize how high the stakes are. That’s why we chose you to be part of this select group for early match access. Facts vs Organized Lying

| | Hi all,

This week I’d like to share a litigation update with regard to some anti-LGBTQ policies recently enacted by several school districts in New Jersey.

**Background**

As you may remember from our June 23 newsletter, school boards in Middletown, Manalapan-Englishtown, and Marlboro recently approved updates to their policies on transgender students and now require school staff to notify parents if their child changes gender identity or expression–regardless of what the student wishes, and despite [evidence that outing students to unreceptive families increases their risk for self-harm, suicide, and homelessness.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68310044/422626208/-1199868712?refcode=EM_NBI_DFD_20230818_OT_news_0_3MO_DG_na_na_newsletter&refcode2=3e53bca2-0a3e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82MzYzOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTUzYmNhMi0wYTNlLWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4A0Pnj1uHZoKl9FYlN5im4Yuew90UP1Y5gV1lhRv2dI=&emci=a274219c-013e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&emdi=3e53bca2-0a3e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&ceid=19214294)

While these school boards claim they are making these changes to secure “parent’s rights” and protect students, the policies were changed despite parents, students, educators, and community members asking them not to do so. **Latest Developments**

Following [a hearing in Monmouth County on Tuesday, August 15](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68310050/422626214/-541491632?refcode=EM_NBI_DFD_20230818_OT_news_0_3MO_DG_na_na_newsletter&refcode2=3e53bca2-0a3e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82MzYzOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTUzYmNhMi0wYTNlLWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4A0Pnj1uHZoKl9FYlN5im4Yuew90UP1Y5gV1lhRv2dI=&emci=a274219c-013e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&emdi=3e53bca2-0a3e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&ceid=19214294), school board members, parent’s rights activists, and LGBTQ+ advocates must wait for the judge to rule on whether the three districts can continue to implement what many view as discriminatory changes.

The hearing allowed lawyers representing the attorney general, the Division of Civil Rights, and the school districts to argue whether the new policies can stand while the litigation is ongoing, or whether the districts should revert to their previous policy, which is more in line with the New Jersey [Department of Education’s guidance for school districts regarding transgender students.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68310051/422626215/1233684113?refcode=EM_NBI_DFD_20230818_OT_news_0_3MO_DG_na_na_newsletter&refcode2=3e53bca2-0a3e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82MzYzOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTUzYmNhMi0wYTNlLWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4A0Pnj1uHZoKl9FYlN5im4Yuew90UP1Y5gV1lhRv2dI=&emci=a274219c-013e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&emdi=3e53bca2-0a3e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&ceid=19214294)

A similar legal process is already underway in Hanover, where AG Platkin filed a similar [civil rights complaint](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68310052/422626216/-17061283?refcode=EM_NBI_DFD_20230818_OT_news_0_3MO_DG_na_na_newsletter&refcode2=3e53bca2-0a3e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82MzYzOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTUzYmNhMi0wYTNlLWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4A0Pnj1uHZoKl9FYlN5im4Yuew90UP1Y5gV1lhRv2dI=&emci=a274219c-013e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&emdi=3e53bca2-0a3e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&ceid=19214294) against the Hanover Board of Education and its public schools, arguing that a new policy requiring schools to notify parents of their child’s gender identity and sexual orientation violates the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination. [In the Hanover case](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68310053/422626217/314012970?refcode=EM_NBI_DFD_20230818_OT_news_0_3MO_DG_na_na_newsletter&refcode2=3e53bca2-0a3e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82MzYzOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTUzYmNhMi0wYTNlLWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4A0Pnj1uHZoKl9FYlN5im4Yuew90UP1Y5gV1lhRv2dI=&emci=a274219c-013e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&emdi=3e53bca2-0a3e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&ceid=19214294), a judge told the attorney general and the Hanover school board to rewrite a rule so it would not discriminate against gay, transgender and nonbinary students.

Arguing on behalf of the school districts, attorney Marc Zitomer argued that notifying parents of a change in their child’s gender identity or expression is not “outing” students or violating a student’s right to privacy.

Arguing on behalf of the state, Deputy Attorney General James Michael said that while the attorney general’s office and the Division of Civil Rights support parents’ rights, it may not be safe for all transgender students to be out to their parents or guardians.

In these cases, mandatory parental notification policies can put students at risk. “We do not oppose and strongly affirm parental rights,” Michael said. He added, however, that parents’ rights must be balanced with a student’s right to go to school safely.

Any discussion of this issue deserves nuance, space, and patience. But I was struck by an observation Grace Byron made in _New York Magazine_ this week, in an article she wrote titled [The False Gospel of Conversion Therapy: I went to sessions every week in high school. I came out as trans anyway:](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68310063/422626227/-1858854770?refcode=EM_NBI_DFD_20230818_OT_news_0_3MO_DG_na_na_newsletter&refcode2=3e53bca2-0a3e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82MzYzOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTUzYmNhMi0wYTNlLWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4A0Pnj1uHZoKl9FYlN5im4Yuew90UP1Y5gV1lhRv2dI=&emci=a274219c-013e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&emdi=3e53bca2-0a3e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&ceid=19214294) “There was one moment where things could’ve gone differently. My sophomore-year art teacher took me aside when she found me sobbing in study hall. I didn’t give her a play by play, but I muddled through what I could say out loud. After my weak explanation, she looked me in the eye and told me I should focus on school. “It’ll get better,” she said.

It did not get better, but I did eventually make it out. At the end of my junior year, I convinced myself and my conversion therapist that I could be celibate. The sin was the practice, not the identity. I came out in college as gay in spite of the lingering fear I was evil. My college was only about 50 miles from home. After reading Mary Oliver poems and watching Laverne Cox talk, I sent a long letter to my parents explaining everything, and my mom decided to reach back out to my conversion therapist. He told her I was going to go to hell.

Eventually, he sent my mother another message: “I’m sorry I said that. My wife has cancer.”

Many years went by before me and my parents could even broach the subject. We didn’t have the same emotional facts.” _We didn’t have the same emotional facts._

I think this lies at the heart of our school board–and political–battles today. As Hannah Arendt wrote in her 1967 essay, [Truth and Politics](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68310064/422626228/-943799241?refcode=EM_NBI_DFD_20230818_OT_news_0_3MO_DG_na_na_newsletter&refcode2=3e53bca2-0a3e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82MzYzOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTUzYmNhMi0wYTNlLWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4A0Pnj1uHZoKl9FYlN5im4Yuew90UP1Y5gV1lhRv2dI=&emci=a274219c-013e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&emdi=3e53bca2-0a3e-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&ceid=19214294), facts are the product of a community living and acting together, whose function is to provide a common understanding of the world.

As Arendt also observes, facts are always vulnerable to “organized lying”–as we are seeing repeatedly from extremist school board candidates and right-wing organizations intent on undermining public education.

The aim of organized liars is not just to replace a part of the truth with a falsehood; they want to undermine the factual fabric of a commonly shared reality (or, as Steve Bannon famously said, “to flood the zone with shit”).

Through organized lying, facts are gradually downgraded to mere matters of opinion, which gives the organized liar three advantages: (1) to say things and then claim they never did; (2) to rewrite history in order to serve their interests; (3) to call specific groups (e.g., trans students, BOE rivals, librarians, teachers) a threat, without the need to back it up by evidence.

All this speaks to the enormous importance of public institutions such as libraries, schools, and universities. These are places where facts are conserved and the public record is maintained. Without them, we would lose an important pillar protecting factual truth.

Which is why it is essential we protect our public schools.

**What Can You Do to Support Good BOE Candidates?**

As I wrote last week, quoting Winn Khuong of BoardBOOST, “It’s simple: Do or donate.” Whether it’s a few hours or a few dollars, this is what the far right is doing for its candidates and we need to follow suit.

Over the next few weeks we will share a list of races we’re working to support. These candidates will need volunteers, donors, and word of mouth. Until then, find out who is running in your town and reach out. We’re stronger together, and standing up for what we believe in is more powerful when we stand together.

And of course, a shortcut is to support our work here at Districts for Democracy.

Thank you all again for your attention, and your time. Together we’re going to keep New Jersey public schools number one in the nation.

Sincerely,

Darcy
Executive Director

Hello, On this day in 1920, the 19th Amendment, which granted women the constitutional right to vote, was ratified. I have immense gratitude for the generations of women who paved the way to expand voting rights through years of organizing — and as the first woman to represent Illinois’ 13th district, I’m proud to be an example for the next generation of young women and encourage them to become politically involved. Even though we’ve come a long way over the last 103 years, I would be remiss if I didn’t say that our work to achieve true democracy is far from over. Despite the passage of the 19th Amendment, people of color, including women of color, are still denied the right to vote today through coordinated voter suppression tactics. GOP-led state legislatures have targeted Black and brown folks across our country by passing restrictive voting laws that limit their ability to vote by mail, cutting early voting hours, purging voters from the voter rolls, and even criminalizing organizers who hand out water to voters waiting in line in some states. I am committed to making progress in our fight to expand and protect the fundamental right to vote for every American, but I need to know your standing with me in this fight. name: Sen. Heidi Campbell
subject: Monday's special session
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Campbell for State Senate, Chip Forrester, treasurer
body:
https://www.voteheidicampbell.com/ [https://www.voteheidicampbell.com/]
Peter,
Back in April in the aftermath of the devastating Covenant shooting Governor Lee called on the legislature to pass red flag laws and indicated his intent to call a special session to address the horrible public health crisis that has been catalyzed by the passage of some of the most relaxed gun laws in the country.
On Monday at 4pm the special session will convene, but there is no mention of guns in the call. Instead, the Governor has called on legislators to pass laws to increase punishments for juvenile offenders, to criminalize mental health, and to militarize our communities.
Since we gaveled out of session last April there have been: [https://tnunderthegun.wixsite.com/tn-under-the-gun/post-session-shootings]
*
Shooting
incidents:
470
[https://tnunderthegun.wixsite.com/tn-under-the-gun/post-session-shootings]
*
Mass
shootings:
7
[https://tnunderthegun.wixsite.com/tn-under-the-gun/post-session-shootings]
*
Adults
killed:
180
[https://tnunderthegun.wixsite.com/tn-under-the-gun/post-session-shootings]
*
Adults
injured:
351
[https://tnunderthegun.wixsite.com/tn-under-the-gun/post-session-shootings]
*
Children
killed:
24
[https://tnunderthegun.wixsite.com/tn-under-the-gun/post-session-shootings]
*
Children
injured:
38
[https://tnunderthegun.wixsite.com/tn-under-the-gun/post-session-shootings]
*
Firearm
suicides:
262
[https://tnunderthegun.wixsite.com/tn-under-the-gun/post-session-shootings]
Over 80% of Tennesseans (with a majority of Republicans) [https://www.tennessean.com/story/news/health/2023/04/17/exclusive-survey-finds-strong-bipartisan-support-for-gun-safety-red-flag-laws-tennessee/70116695007/] support strengthening background checks for firearm purchases. Members of the controlling party are placing their own political interests over the safety of Tennesseans.
I am sponsoring several bills that fit within the extreme limits of the special session. Because 2.2 Tennesseans use a gun to take their own life everyday and over half of all gun deaths in our state are suicides, my office has filed:
*
The
Tennessee
Voluntary
Do
Not
Sell
Firearms
Act,
which
would
allow
individuals
to
voluntarily
and
confidentially
restrict
immediate
access
to
firearm
purchases.
I
have
worked
with
suicide
prevention
organizations
and
legal
experts
to
draft
a
bill
that
mirrors
legislation
that
passed
in
other
states
with
the
support
of
both
Democrats
and
Republicans.
*
A
resolution
promoting
and
encouraging
the
use
of
the
national
988
suicide
prevention
hotline
number.
Additionally, I have filed a bill to increase the number of licensed school counselors in Tennessee elementary, middle, and high schools so that we can bring our counselor to student ratio closer to what is recommended by national school counselor organizations. This legislation is supported by the Tennessee School Counselors Association who have been instrumental in drafting it.
Our caucus will also take advantage of this opportunity to run bills for medicaid expansion, deadlines for the TBI, school safety plans prohibiting guns on property, gun locks required to be provided with gun purchases, department of health to report data on gun deaths, and for the Department of Education to seek grants for gun violence prevention.
We will be pushing back and speaking out against legislation that seeks to increase our school-to-prison pipeline, to criminalize mental health, and to arm teachers. While this is not the session we had hoped for, we will continue to work towards passing laws that keep our children and families safe. We also intend to file a comprehensive slate of evidence-based gun law reform legislation in 2024.
If you plan to come down to the capitol during the special session, please stop by my office. I’d love to see you, and don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or suggestions. My cell is 615.438.6338.
All my best,
Heidi

Additionally, I have filed a bill to increase the number of licensed school counselors in Tennessee elementary, middle, and high schools so that we can bring our counselor to student ratio closer to what is recommended by national school counselor organizations. This legislation is supported by the Tennessee School Counselors Association who have been instrumental in drafting it. Our caucus will also take advantage of this opportunity to run bills for medicaid expansion, deadlines for the TBI, school safety plans prohibiting guns on property, gun locks required to be provided with gun purchases, department of health to report data on gun deaths, and for the Department of Education to seek grants for gun violence prevention. We will be pushing back and speaking out against legislation that seeks to increase our school-to-prison pipeline, to criminalize mental health, and to arm teachers. While this is not the session we had hoped for, we will continue to work towards passing laws that keep our children and families safe. We also intend to file a comprehensive slate of evidence-based gun law reform legislation in 2024. If you plan to come down to the capitol during the special session, please stop by my office. I’d love to see you, and don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or suggestions. My cell is 615.438.6338. All my best, Heidi [] [] [] Paid for by Campbell for State Senate, Chip Forrester, treasurer. name: Katie Porter
subject: re: answering your questions!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Katie Porter for Senate
body:
Using a few minutes to look over your questions
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/14558?t=1&akid=28408%2E3422442%2ElDJsWG)
A few weeks back my team asked what questions you have for me—I have a few minutes between campaign stops today, so I wanted to answer a few:
From Wendy in McCloud, CA: _Why is mental health treated like something invisible instead of a medical problem?_
Big Insurance companies don’t want to pay for mental healthcare. Back in 2020, I introduced the**Mental Health Parity Compliance Act to strengthen enforcement of the federal law that requires insurance companies to cover mental health the same way they cover other types of care.** Just last month, I joined President Biden in the White House as he announced new steps to implement my law to finally force insurance companies to treat mental health care like physical care. **This is an oversight and enforcement issue,** and I’ll always stand up to Big Insurance companies when they try to cheat patients who desperately need care.
---
From Gerald in Nampa, ID: _How can we get money out of Congress?_
First and foremost, we have to overturn _Citizens United_ , the Supreme Court case that has allowed money to flood our political system. But that’s not going to happen in the immediate term, so **right now leading by example is important.** I’ve made the choice to be one of fewer than a dozen House Members to reject both corporate PAC and federal lobbyist money. I also started an organization called Truth to Power, funded by grassroots donors, to help elect other Democrats who reject corporate PAC money. We also need big structural change which will come through legislation. **I helped pass legislation through the House that would have cracked down on dark money in politics, but unfortunately it failed in the Senate.** I agree that the insane amount of money in our political system is a huge problem, and rooting out corruption is one of my top priorities.
---
From Randall in Palo Alto, CA: _How exactly, (and give examples please), can you be more effective in the Senate than you are currently in the House?_
Great question. Senators sit on twice as many committees as House members, so I’d be able to work on more issues and have ***double* the hearings where I can get answers from CEOs or government officials.** Senators are 1/100, rather than 1/435, so I’d have **more influence to push for policies that don’t get talked about enough in the Senate, like paid family leave, lowering the cost of child care, and addressing the skyrocketing cost of housing.**
---
Thanks, everyone, for all the questions! We got more than 500 of them, and I truly wish I could chat with all of you.
Thanks for being on Team Porter.
Katie
[**P.S. The only way I’ll win this race is with grassroots support. Can you chip in $5 today?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4s-em-20230818-2?amount=5&refcode=EMAK18_2_ANS_20230818_V1_F&refcode2=28408_3422442_lDJsWG&akid=28408%2E3422442%2ElDJsWG)

Katie is running for the U.S. Senate because Californians deserve a warrior fighting for them in Washington. Our campaign is people-powered, we don’t take a dime from corporate PACs, federal lobbyists, or executives from Big Oil or Big Pharma. **[Donate ›››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4s-em-footer?refcode=EMAK18_2_ANS_20230818_V1_F&t=2&refcode2=28408_3422442_lDJsWG&akid=28408%2E3422442%2ElDJsWG)**

* Don’t whack each other with pool noodles

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Supporting Maui
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
Once you’ve donated, please share this email with your network of friends and family to help boost our collective mutual aid efforts.
#
Peter,
By now, many of us have seen the devastation and destruction that has taken place in Lahaina Town, Maui. As of this week, more than 111 people have died from the Maui wildfires, and it is expected that we’ll see a rise in that number over time.
Peter, now more than ever, we must show up for our Maui neighbors and do everything we can to support their community as they work to heal and rebuild.
Our team has compiled a list of mutual aid organizations and groups who are on the ground supporting Maui residents with food, resources, and security. If you are able, please consider contributing to one or all of these resources.
**Once you’re finished, please share this email with your network of friends and family to help boost our collective efforts.
* _Maui Just Recovery Fund_
**

Hosted by the Amalgamated Foundation, the Maui Just Recovery Fund supports immediate relief efforts to house, feed, and support displaced families and dedicate resources for the long term effects to rebuild and advance structural changes.
**[Click here to donate to the Maui Just Recovery Fund:](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/44644?refcode=em20230818-2829&t=1&akid=2829%2E420207%2EVNyMVj)**
**[Donate ››](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/44644?refcode=em20230818-2829&t=2&akid=2829%2E420207%2EVNyMVj)**
* _**Maui Fire Relief + Recovery Fundraiser_
**

The Maui Fire Relief + Recovery Fundraiser is working with the community to organize and establish supply hubs, conduct regular wellness checks, advocate for additional FEMA and state assistance, form durable community power, and keep Hawaiian lands in Hawaiian hands.
**[Click here to donate to the Maui Fire Relief + Recovery Fundraiser:](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/44645?refcode=em20230818-2829&t=3&akid=2829%2E420207%2EVNyMVj)**
**[Donate ››](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/44645?refcode=em20230818-2829&t=4&akid=2829%2E420207%2EVNyMVj)**
* _**Emergency Fundraiser for Maui Fires_
**

‘Āina Momona is supporting the [ Hawaii Community Foundation Maui County Strong Fund](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/44646?refcode=em20230818-2829&t=5&akid=2829%2E420207%2EVNyMVj) to support disaster relief on Maui. Their goal is to provide financial resources that can be deployed quickly, with a focus on rapid response and recovery for the devastating wildfires.
**[Click here to donate to the Emergency Fundraiser for Maui Fires:](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/44647?refcode=em20230818-2829&t=6&akid=2829%2E420207%2EVNyMVj)**
**[Donate ››](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/44647?refcode=em20230818-2829&t=7&akid=2829%2E420207%2EVNyMVj)**
Again, please consider donating to support Maui and Hawaiians who are mitigating the devastating aftermath of these wildfires. And please share this email with your network to help boost our collective mutual aid efforts in light of these events.
With love and in solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

Friend,

Today marks the 103rd anniversary of the ratification of the 19th Amendment: The landmark amendment which extended suffrage to women across the country.

**However, 103 years later, we still find ourselves pushing for equal representation **and fighting for women to have a seat at the table – especially within the marginalized communities for whom enfranchisement didn't come for decades after the 19th Amendment.

Even in the 118th Congress – where a record-breaking number of women are serving – women only comprise 28% of the members.
